lesson_title: Databases & Transactions — SQL Basics and ACID

questions.question: Why does this SQL UPDATE not change any rows even though the WHERE looks correct?
questions.code: UPDATE booking SET remainingsessions = remainingsessions - 1 WHERE booking_id = '123';
options: The booking_id column is numeric, but the query uses a string literal — types must match or be cast
UPDATE queries cannot use WHERE clauses
remainingsessions cannot be decremented without a transaction
The table name must be quoted with double quotes

questions.question: What is the main guarantee provided by a database transaction's ACID properties?
options: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — grouped operations behave as one unit
Automatic Caching, Inline Delivery
Asynchronous Calls, Cached Data
Aggregated, Concurrent, Isolated, Distributed

questions.question: Why is this LEFT JOIN returning more rows than expected?
questions.code: SELECT s.s_id, s.name, b.booking_id FROM student s LEFT JOIN booking b ON s.s_id = b.s_id WHERE b.plan_id = 2;
options: The WHERE clause converts the LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN because it filters on the joined table — move the condition into the JOIN or use OR b.plan_id IS NULL
LEFT JOINs always duplicate rows by design
plan_id must be in the SELECT to work
You must use DISTINCT with LEFT JOINs

questions.question: Which SQL clause limits rows returned after aggregation?
options: HAVING
WHERE
GROUP BY
ORDER BY

questions.question: Why does this transaction still show partially applied changes to another connection?
questions.code:
BEGIN; UPDATE booking SET remainingsessions = remainingsessions - 1 WHERE booking_id=5; -- long work here
-- other connection reads booking.remainingsessions and sees new value before COMMIT
options: Isolation level may be READ UNCOMMITTED — increase isolation or use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock rows
Transactions require explicit ROLLBACK to be visible
You must call COMMIT before the other connection can connect
Updates are eventually consistent and should be polled

questions.question: Which index type is best when you need exact equality lookups on a unique id?
options: B-tree index
Full-text index
GIN index
Hash index for all workloads

questions.question: What is wrong in this migration snippet that creates a foreign key?
questions.code: ALTER TABLE session ADD CONSTRAINT fk_teacher FOREIGN KEY (t_id) REFERENCES teacher(uid);
options: REFERENCES target column types must match; teacher.uid is text while session.t_id is integer — reference teacher.t_id instead
Foreign keys cannot be added after table creation
You must DROP constraints before adding new ones
CONSTRAINT names cannot include underscore

questions.question: Which statement best describes an idempotent database operation?
options: Applying the operation multiple times has the same effect as applying it once
The operation always returns the same result regardless of input
Idempotent operations are faster than others
They are only supported by NoSQL databases

questions.question: Why can this bulk insert be slow and how to improve it?
questions.code: for (const row of rows) { await db.insert('booking').values(row); }
options: Inserting in a loop issues many separate transactions — use a single bulk insert or batch and wrap in one transaction
Await inside for is fine; slowness is from network latency only
Use JSON columns instead of rows to speed up inserts
You must call COMMIT after each insert for performance

questions.question: Which is a common strategy to avoid deadlocks in transactional code?
options: Access resources in a consistent order across code paths
Open many transactions concurrently
Use random backoff without retries
Disable indexes before transactions
